prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on incoming string values for any field whose annotation isn't exactly `str`, including str-containing unions like `str | None`. members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the task group spawns post_writer and the caller proceeds (or starts the GET stream) before post_writer has actually entered its read loop, so a message sent on write_stream immediately after can be missed. Both PRs fix it identically — adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and calling `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context, so the caller can `tg.start()` and block until post_writer is truly ready.

clusters.pick_reason: 2478's _restore_mcp_error dispatches generically across the whole MCPError hierarchy (exc_type.from_error_data), with an explicit special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError (exc_type.from_error) covering the exact scenario 2555 fixes, and it also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on MCPError.data, indicating the base-class payload path is now exercised by tests too. 2555's fix is a hand-written __reduce__ scoped only to UrlElicitationRequiredError, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-default constructor signature would still hit the same TypeError after 2555 merges — 2478 closes that gap for the entire hierarchy in one change rather than one subclass.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Pickling an MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) raises TypeError on unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args = (code, message, data) doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None). clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the same two except blocks in utils.py with `from e`. #2777 additionally drops the redundant f-string interpolation of `{e}` in the raised message (e.g. `raise OAuthRegistrationError("Invalid registration response") from e` instead of embedding the exception text in the message), avoiding duplicate error text now that `from e` already surfaces the original exception in the traceback. #2565 keeps the old interpolated message alongside the new `from e`, so it's a narrower, less complete version of the same fix.
